title: Detecting Rising Wildfire Risks for South East England
content:
In July 2022 southeast England experienced a record breaking heatwave and unprecedented wildfires in urban areas. We investigate fire weather trends since 1960 in southeast England using a large ensemble of initialised climate models. We show that between the 1960's and 2010's annual maximum daily fire weather has increased, with a halving of the return period of a high risk day from a 1-in-4 year event in the 1960s to a 1-in-2 year event in the last decade.

Modelled change in daily fire weather risk for South East England. Showing the percentage change between the past (1961–1970) and present (2013–2022) of total summertime days within each fire danger class, using the large ensemble of initialised climate model data.


ABSTRACT

In July 2022 southeast England experienced a record breaking heatwave and unprecedented wildfires in urban areas. We investigate fire weather trends since 1960 in southeast England using a large ensemble of initialised climate models. Record smashing temperatures coincided with widespread fires in London, and we find that while wildfire risk was high, it was not record breaking. We show that between the 1960s and 2010s annual maximum daily fire weather has increased. The proportion of summertime days with high and very high fire risk has increased—while medium and low risk days have become less common. These findings show the need to mitigate against the increasing risk of wildfire caused by climate change.
